summary: The transition-hook reentrancy hazard also applies to recursive `step`, not only register/unregister. With zero hold/cooldown, an outer F0->F4 step can invoke a callback that recursively steps the same entity F0->F4 with a successful inner hook. The inner step commits the count/state transition, then the outer step commits the same transition a second time, producing negative F0 and duplicate F4 accounting for one registered entity. Test-adversary head 952f6a02c9810ae054f7bb4b040e2d64666222c2 adds a contract-neutral aggregate-accounting invariant for this exact double-commit path. Any in-flight mutation guard must therefore cover `step` as well as `register` and `unregister`; read-only manager APIs can remain callable from transition hooks.
evidence: FidelityManager.step invokes arbitrary applyTransition before outer count/state commit and currently has no in-flight reentrancy guard.
A recursively successful inner step observes the same pre-commit F0 state and commits F0->F4; outer step then repeats the same count mutation.
The added test only requires all counts to remain non-negative and sum to registered, so either fail-closed reentrancy rejection or another atomic design can satisfy it.
